errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics. The factual claims in the clipping (not Hilbert's own) are loose:
Rossini wrote the Petite messe solennelle in 1863 at age 71, not 72.
Bismarck organised the Norddeutscher Bund (1866/67) at about 51–52, not the 'Deutscher Bund' (that was the 1815 Confederation).
Gladstone's last premiership began in 1892, when he was 82, so 'still at 80' is understated but defensible.
Ito (born 1841) at 65 corresponds to about 1906, his Korea Resident-Generalship; his major Meiji reforms (constitution of 1889) came much earlier.
'Solenelle' is a misspelling in the clipping itself.

deep.surprise_reason: There is no mathematical content. The page is of modest biographical and historical interest, mainly the late-1930s list 'Hitlers Verdienste', which bears on discussions of Hilbert's political attitudes. However, its status (Hilbert's own view versus noted opinion) is unclear, and it says nothing about mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Rossini's age when composing the Petite messe solennelle (1863) was 71, not 72 as the clipping says
Bismarck's age at the founding of the Norddeutscher Bund (1867) was about 52
Gladstone's age at the start of his fourth premiership was 83 by year difference (82 at the actual date), i.e. over 80
'20 years after the end of the war' (previous page) dates these notes to about 1938

transcription_corrections: 'Eicken[?]' is correct: the author is Heinrich von Eicken, whose 'Geschichte und System der mittelalterlichen Weltanschauung' appeared with Cotta, Stuttgart, 1887.
'Unbillen[?]' appears correct as read ('Beseitigung der Unbillen d. Versailler Vertrages').
The Zurich line uses ditto marks; in full it reads 'In Zürich bin ich Ehrendoktor'.
The Danzig line is 'In Danzig ?', with the question mark written slightly raised.
